prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a rectangular box resting on a flat ground line, with one straight arrow of equal length pushing it from the left and one equal straight arrow pushing it from the right, and one arrow pointing down from the box and one equal arrow pointing up from the ground. Plain single-line arrows with open heads, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: box, ground line, left push arrow, right push arrow, downward weight arrow, upward support arrow.
subject: physics
why: shown whenever a lesson introduces balanced forces and why an object stays still or keeps constant speed

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a rectangular box on a flat ground line with a long straight arrow pushing it to the right and a much shorter straight arrow pushing it to the left, and a short curved motion streak behind the box showing it moving right. Plain single-line arrows with open heads, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: box, ground line, long push arrow, short opposing arrow, motion streak.
subject: physics
why: the paired picture to balanced forces, used whenever resultant force and acceleration are introduced

prompt: A simple unlabelled free body force diagram: a plain rectangular block sitting on a horizontal ground line, with four straight single-line arrows drawn from the centre of the block pointing up, down, left and right. Arrows are clearly separated and of different lengths. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: block, ground line, weight arrow, normal contact arrow, applied force arrow, friction arrow.
subject: physics
why: the standard four-arrow free body diagram every forces question is built on

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a round ball falling through the air, with one long straight arrow pointing down from the ball and one shorter straight arrow pointing up from the ball, plus a few short speed streaks above it. No ground, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: falling ball, downward weight arrow, upward air resistance arrow, speed streaks.
subject: physics
why: used for falling objects, air resistance and the build-up to terminal velocity

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a right-angled triangular ramp with a plain rectangular block resting on its sloping surface. One straight arrow points vertically down from the block, one straight arrow points away from the slope at right angles to it, and one straight arrow points up along the slope surface. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: ramp, block, weight arrow, normal contact arrow, friction arrow.
subject: physics
why: the slope free body diagram used for ramps, friction and resolving forces

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a block sliding on a surface, with a circular magnified inset showing the two touching surfaces enormously enlarged as jagged interlocking bumps. A straight arrow shows the block's motion and an opposing straight arrow points backwards at the contact point. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: sliding block, flat surface, magnifier circle, rough surface bumps, motion arrow, friction arrow.
subject: physics
why: explains why friction exists at all, reused in forces, energy and machines chapters

prompt: A simple unlabelled line graph: two plain axes meeting at the origin, with three separate straight or curved lines drawn on them - one flat horizontal line, one straight sloping line, and one upward-bending curve. No numbers, no tick labels, no words anywhere. Clean thin lines. Name the layer groups exactly: horizontal axis, vertical axis, flat line, straight sloping line, upward curve.
subject: physics
why: the graph a teacher draws for stationary, steady speed and accelerating motion

prompt: A simple unlabelled line graph: two plain axes meeting at the origin, with a straight line rising from the origin, then a flat horizontal section, then a straight line falling back to the axis, and the area beneath the shape marked out with light hatching. No numbers, no tick labels, no words. Clean thin lines. Name the layer groups exactly: horizontal axis, vertical axis, rising line, flat line, falling line, area under the graph.
subject: physics
why: used for acceleration from gradient and distance from the area under the line

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram showing the same falling skydiver figure drawn three times down the page: first with a long down arrow and a tiny up arrow, then with arrows closer in length, then with an open parachute above the figure and a long up arrow and short down arrow. Plain outline figure, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: skydiver figure, open parachute, downward weight arrow, upward air resistance arrow.
subject: physics
why: the picture for terminal velocity, drag and how a parachute changes the force balance

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of two simple standing figures facing each other with their palms touching, each with a straight arrow pointing away from the other showing them pushing apart, and short motion streaks behind each figure. Plain outline figures, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: left figure, right figure, left push arrow, right push arrow, motion streaks.
subject: physics
why: the everyday picture for action and reaction force pairs

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a car in side view on a straight road line, with two separate bracket spans drawn beneath the road: a short one immediately behind the car's start position and a longer one following it, joined end to end. No shading, no numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: car, road line, thinking distance span, braking distance span, total stopping bracket.
subject: physics
why: the road safety diagram used for reaction time, braking and stopping distance

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a clamp stand holding three identical coiled springs side by side: the first hanging free, the second stretched longer with one slotted mass hanging from it, the third stretched longer still with two slotted masses. A vertical ruler stands beside them with plain unnumbered tick marks. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: clamp stand, unstretched spring, stretched spring, slotted masses, ruler, extension gap.
subject: physics
why: the Hooke's law required practical, reused for elastic behaviour and force-extension graphs

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a straight horizontal beam resting on a triangular pivot placed under its centre, with a small square weight hanging near the left end and a larger square weight hanging closer to the pivot on the right. A horizontal distance arrow runs from the pivot to each weight. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: beam, pivot, left weight, right weight, left distance arrow, right distance arrow.
subject: physics
why: the see-saw picture behind every moments, turning effect and balance calculation

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram showing three straight bars stacked one above the other, each resting on a small triangular pivot: in the top bar the pivot is in the middle, in the middle bar the pivot is at one end with a load near the middle, in the bottom bar the pivot is at one end with an effort arrow near the middle. Each bar has one downward arrow for effort and one downward arrow for load. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: first class lever, second class lever, third class lever, pivot, effort arrow, load arrow.
subject: physics
why: the one picture that carries a whole lesson on lever classes and mechanical advantage

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a wheelbarrow in side view: a single wheel at the front, a shallow tray holding a rounded heap of load, and two long handles at the back. A downward arrow sits on the load and an upward arrow sits at the handle ends. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: wheel, tray, load, handles, effort arrow, load arrow.
subject: physics
why: the everyday second class lever used to make moments feel real

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a pulley system: one grooved pulley wheel fixed to an overhead beam, a second grooved pulley wheel hanging below it carrying a rectangular load, and a single rope threaded around both with its free end pulled downwards by an arrow. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: overhead beam, fixed pulley, movable pulley, rope, load, effort arrow.
subject: physics
why: shown whenever pulleys, mechanical advantage or lifting machines come up

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a right-angled triangular ramp with a rectangular crate part way up the sloping face, an arrow pushing the crate up along the slope, a vertical arrow marking the ramp's height and a horizontal arrow marking its base length. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: ramp, crate, push arrow, height arrow, base length arrow.
subject: physics
why: the simplest machine, used for ramps, work done and force multiplication

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of two identical rectangular blocks resting on a bed of soft sand: the left block lies on its wide flat face and makes a shallow dip, the right block stands on its narrow edge and sinks into a deep narrow dip. A downward arrow of equal length sits above each block. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: wide face block, narrow edge block, sand surface, shallow dip, deep dip, weight arrows.
subject: physics
why: the picture for pressure equals force over area, reused for snowshoes, knives and foundations

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a tall container of water with three small holes down one side, one near the top, one in the middle and one near the bottom, with a curved jet of water arcing out of each hole - shortest from the top hole and longest from the bottom hole. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: container, water surface, top jet, middle jet, bottom jet, depth arrow.
subject: physics
why: the classic demonstration that pressure in a liquid grows with depth

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a rectangular tank of water with a horizontal water surface line: one block floats with part of it above the surface, one block sits exactly level with the surface, and one block lies on the bottom of the tank. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: tank, water surface, floating block, suspended block, sunken block.
subject: physics
why: used whenever density, floating and sinking are compared

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a rectangular block floating in water with part of it above the surface, one straight arrow pointing down from the centre of the block and one equal straight arrow pointing up from underneath it, and a dashed outline showing the submerged part. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: floating block, water surface, submerged part, downward weight arrow, upward upthrust arrow.
subject: physics
why: the force picture behind flotation, upthrust and Archimedes' principle

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a cylindrical can with a short spout near its rim, full of water to the spout, with an irregular stone being lowered into it on a thread and water running out of the spout into a narrow measuring cylinder standing beside it. Plain unnumbered tick marks on the cylinder. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: displacement can, spout, water, stone, measuring cylinder.
subject: physics
why: the standard method for finding the volume of an irregular object when measuring density

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a sealed hydraulic system: a narrow cylinder with a small piston on the left joined by a horizontal pipe to a wide cylinder with a large piston on the right, both cylinders filled with liquid shown as plain horizontal lines. A short downward arrow sits on the small piston and a long upward arrow on the large piston. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: narrow cylinder, small piston, connecting pipe, liquid, wide cylinder, large piston, effort arrow, load arrow.
subject: physics
why: shown for hydraulics, brakes and pressure transmitted through liquids

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a long vertical glass tube standing upside down with its open end below the surface of liquid in a shallow open dish, the tube part filled with liquid, an empty gap at the sealed top, and a vertical height arrow beside the tube from the dish surface to the top of the liquid column. Downward arrows press on the dish surface. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: glass tube, liquid column, vacuum gap, dish of liquid, height arrow, air pressure arrows.
subject: physics
why: the instrument diagram for atmospheric pressure and how it is measured

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of three plain empty rectangular boxes: one on the left, one in the middle and one on the right, joined left to right by two thick straight arrows, with a third arrow branching downwards from the middle box to a fourth empty box below. Boxes are completely empty. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: input store box, device box, useful output box, wasted output box, transfer arrows.
subject: physics
why: the reusable skeleton for any energy transfer chain the lesson needs to fill in

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a Sankey arrow: one wide horizontal band entering from the left, splitting into a narrow band that continues straight to the right and a much wider band that bends downwards, each band drawn as a plain outline with straight edges and an arrowhead at its end. No shading, no numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: input band, useful output band, wasted output band, branch point.
subject: physics
why: the standard efficiency picture, reused for lamps, motors and power stations

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a pendulum: a fixed pivot at the top with a string hanging from it and a round bob, drawn three times - swung high to the left, hanging straight down at the bottom, and swung high to the right - with a dashed arc showing the path and a horizontal dashed line at the lowest point. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: pivot, string, bob at the left, bob at the lowest point, bob at the right, swing arc.
subject: physics
why: the picture for kinetic and gravitational potential store swapping back and forth

prompt: A simple unlabelled line drawing of a roller coaster track in side view: a tall first hill, a deep dip, a lower second hill and a final dip, with a small cart drawn on the top of the first hill and a dashed height line from the track up to each hilltop. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: track, tall first hill, lowest dip, lower second hill, cart, height lines.
subject: physics
why: the favourite context for energy conservation and height against speed

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a simple standing figure lifting a rectangular box from the ground to above their head, with a dashed outline of the box at ground level, a vertical arrow showing how far it moved, and a straight upward arrow on the box showing the lifting force. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: figure, box, starting position outline, height arrow, lifting force arrow, ground line.
subject: physics
why: the picture for work done equals force times distance, and for power when time is added

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a thermal power station in cross-section, drawn left to right: a furnace with a flame, a boiler with pipes above it, a bladed turbine wheel, a round generator drum joined to the turbine by a shaft, and a transformer box with a cable leaving to a pylon. Arrows connect each stage. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: furnace, boiler, turbine, generator, transformer, pylon.
subject: physics
why: used in energy resources, electricity generation and the national grid

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram showing four separate energy devices side by side on a ground line: a three-bladed wind turbine on a tower, a flat rectangular solar panel tilted on a stand, a curved dam wall holding back water with an outlet at its base, and a sun with straight rays above them all. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: wind turbine, solar panel, hydroelectric dam, sun, ground line.
subject: physics
why: one picture that carries the whole renewable resources comparison lesson

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a round ball dropped from a hand, with a dashed curved path showing it bouncing three times off a horizontal ground line, each bounce rising to a lower height than the last, and a dashed horizontal height line at the top of each bounce. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: ball, ground line, first bounce, second bounce, third bounce, height lines.
subject: physics
why: shows energy dissipated to the surroundings without needing any equations

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a smooth continuous wavy curve with two full waves, drawn about a straight horizontal dashed centre line, with a vertical arrow from the centre line up to a peak, a horizontal arrow spanning from one peak to the next, and small dots marking the highest and lowest points. No shading, no numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: crest, trough, rest line, amplitude arrow, wavelength arrow.
subject: physics
why: the wave every waves chapter starts from: crest, trough, amplitude and wavelength

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a long horizontal coiled spring drawn as a row of vertical lines, with the lines bunched tightly together in two places and spread widely apart between them, a hand pushing the left end, and a horizontal arrow showing the direction the wave travels. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: coiled spring, compression, rarefaction, hand, wave direction arrow.
subject: physics
why: the slinky picture for longitudinal waves and for how sound travels

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a ripple tank in three-quarter view: a shallow rectangular tray of water on legs, a straight bar dipper suspended just touching the water surface, a lamp above the tray, straight parallel wave lines across the water, and a plain screen below the tray. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: water tray, straight dipper, lamp, wave fronts, screen.
subject: physics
why: the apparatus every wave behaviour demonstration is set up in

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram seen from above: a straight barrier across the picture with a narrow gap in the middle, straight parallel wave lines approaching the barrier from the left, and curved semicircular wave lines spreading out from the gap on the right. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: barrier, gap, straight wave fronts, curved wave fronts, direction arrow.
subject: physics
why: the standard diffraction picture, reused for water, sound and radio waves

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of four separate wavy curves stacked one above the other in a column, each drawn about its own straight horizontal dashed centre line: a tall wave with few waves, a short wave with few waves, a tall wave with many closely spaced waves, and a short wave with many closely spaced waves. No shading, no numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: large amplitude wave, small amplitude wave, high frequency wave, low frequency wave, rest lines.
subject: physics
why: the comparison used for loud and quiet, high and low pitch, and bright and dim

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of one long horizontal rectangular strip divided by vertical lines into seven equal sections in a row, with a wavy line running along beneath the strip whose waves are very long and stretched at the left end and become very short and tightly packed towards the right end, and a long horizontal arrow beneath. No shading, no numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: radio band, microwave band, infrared band, visible band, ultraviolet band, x-ray band, gamma band, wavelength wave.
subject: physics
why: the spine of every electromagnetic waves lesson, reused for uses and dangers

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a cone loudspeaker in side view on the left facing right, with vertical lines in the air in front of it that are bunched closely together in two bands and widely spaced between them, and a simple outline of an ear on the right. A horizontal arrow shows the direction of travel. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: loudspeaker cone, compression, rarefaction, ear, direction arrow.
subject: physics
why: connects vibration, longitudinal wave and hearing in one picture

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of two identical rectangular oscilloscope screens side by side, each ruled with a faint square grid: the left screen shows a wavy trace with tall widely spaced waves, the right screen shows a wavy trace with short closely spaced waves. Plain screen outlines with control knobs omitted. No shading, no numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: left screen, right screen, grid, tall slow trace, short fast trace.
subject: physics
why: how loudness and pitch are read off a trace, used in sound and waves practicals

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a simple standing figure on the left facing a tall vertical cliff face on the right, with curved wave arcs travelling from the figure's mouth towards the cliff and a second set of curved wave arcs travelling back from the cliff towards the figure, and straight arrows on each set showing direction. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: figure, cliff face, outgoing sound waves, reflected sound waves, ground line.
subject: physics
why: the picture for echoes, reflection of sound and speed of sound calculations

prompt: A simple unlabelled cross-section line drawing of a human ear: the outer flap, a tube leading inwards, a taut membrane across the end of the tube, three small linked bones beyond it, a spiral coiled chamber, and a nerve leaving the spiral. Clean outlines with clearly separated parts, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: outer ear, ear canal, eardrum, small bones, cochlea, auditory nerve.
subject: physics
why: used for hearing, hearing range and hearing damage in both physics and biology

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a glass bell jar standing on a flat base plate, with an electric bell hanging inside it on thin threads, wires passing through the base to a cell outside, and a short pipe from the base plate leading to a vacuum pump. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: bell jar, electric bell, base plate, wires, cell, vacuum pump.
subject: physics
why: the demonstration that sound needs a medium, drawn in every sound chapter

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a straight horizontal mirror line with short hatching lines along its back, a dashed line standing at right angles to the mirror at one point, one straight ray arriving at that point from the upper left with an arrowhead, and one straight ray leaving the same point to the upper right with an arrowhead, with a small arc marking the angle on each side of the dashed line. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: mirror, normal, incident ray, reflected ray, angle of incidence, angle of reflection.
subject: physics
why: the law of reflection diagram, used in mirrors, periscopes and every ray practical

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a vertical mirror line with hatching on its back, an upright arrow object standing to the left of it, a mirrored upright arrow drawn in dashed line the same distance behind the mirror, two solid rays going from the object to the mirror and reflecting to an eye, and dashed lines continuing behind the mirror to the dashed arrow. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: mirror, object arrow, virtual image arrow, reflected rays, construction lines, eye.
subject: physics
why: shows why a mirror image is virtual, upright and as far behind as the object is in front

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a rectangular glass block drawn as a plain outline, with a straight ray arriving at its top surface from the upper left, bending as it crosses into the block, travelling as a straight line inside, then bending again as it leaves the bottom surface and continuing away parallel to the first ray. Dashed lines stand at right angles to the surface at each crossing point. Arrowheads on each ray, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: glass block, incident ray, refracted ray, emergent ray, normals.
subject: physics
why: the core refraction diagram, reused for bending of light, angles and refractive index

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a semicircular glass block drawn as a plain outline with its flat side uppermost, three straight rays entering through the curved edge and meeting the same point on the flat surface at different angles: one passing out bending away, one skimming along the flat surface, and one reflecting back down inside the block. A dashed line stands at right angles to the flat surface. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: glass block, flat boundary, normal, refracted ray, grazing ray, totally reflected ray.
subject: physics
why: the picture for the critical angle and total internal reflection

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a long gently curving fibre drawn as two parallel outlines with a thin outer sleeve line on each side, and a straight ray entering one end and zig-zagging along inside by bouncing off the inner walls several times before leaving the far end. Arrowheads on the ray, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: fibre core, cladding, light ray, reflection points.
subject: physics
why: the application diagram for total internal reflection, endoscopes and communications

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a convex lens drawn as a tall thin oval standing on a straight horizontal dashed axis, with an upright arrow object to the left of it, small crosses marked on the axis on each side of the lens, two straight rays leaving the top of the object and passing through the lens to meet at a point on the right, and an inverted arrow drawn where they meet. Arrowheads on each ray, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: converging lens, principal axis, object arrow, focal points, rays, image arrow.
subject: physics
why: the ray construction every lens, camera and eye question depends on

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a concave lens drawn as a tall shape with two inward-curving sides standing on a straight horizontal dashed axis, with an upright arrow object to the left, two straight rays leaving the top of the object and spreading apart after the lens, and dashed lines traced back from the spreading rays meeting at a point where a smaller upright arrow is drawn. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: diverging lens, principal axis, object arrow, spreading rays, construction lines, virtual image arrow.
subject: physics
why: the counterpart to the converging lens, needed for short sight correction

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a curved mirror drawn as an arc opening to the left with short hatching lines on its back, a straight horizontal dashed axis through its centre, an upright arrow object on the axis, a cross marked on the axis in front of the mirror, two straight rays from the top of the object striking the mirror and reflecting to cross at a point, and an inverted arrow drawn there. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: concave mirror, principal axis, object arrow, focal point, reflected rays, image arrow.
subject: physics
why: curved mirror construction, used for headlamps, dishes and telescope mirrors

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a triangular glass prism drawn as a plain outline, with a single narrow straight ray entering one sloping face from the left and a fan of several straight rays spreading out from the opposite face at slightly different angles and landing on a plain vertical screen on the right as a band of narrow parallel strips. No shading, no colour. Name the layer groups exactly: prism, white light ray, spreading rays, screen, spectrum band.
subject: physics
why: the picture for dispersion, the visible spectrum and how a rainbow forms

prompt: A simple unlabelled cross-section line drawing of a human eyeball: a round outer wall, a clear bulge at the front, a ring with a round opening at its centre, a lens shape just behind the opening, a curved inner lining across the back, and a thick nerve leaving the back of the eye. Clean separated outlines, no shading. Name the layer groups exactly: cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina, optic nerve.
subject: physics
why: shared between light, lenses and biology; drawn in every eye and vision lesson

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of two eyeball cross-sections one above the other: in the top one two parallel rays enter and cross at a point clearly in front of the curved back wall; in the bottom one the same rays first pass through a lens with two inward-curving sides placed in front of the eye and then cross exactly on the back wall. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: eyeball, retina, light rays, focus point, concave correcting lens.
subject: physics
why: the standard sight defect and correction diagram, paired with long sight

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a closed rectangular box in cross-section with a tiny hole in the middle of its left wall and a plain screen forming its right wall, an upright candle standing outside to the left, and two straight rays from the top and bottom of the candle crossing at the hole and landing on the screen to form a small upside-down candle shape. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: box, pinhole, candle, light rays, screen, inverted image.
subject: physics
why: shows light travelling in straight lines and how a real inverted image forms

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a broad lamp on the left, a solid rectangular object standing in the middle, and a plain vertical screen on the right, with straight rays drawn from the top and bottom of the lamp past both edges of the object to the screen, producing a dark central band on the screen with a lighter band above and below it. No shading beyond plain outlines. Name the layer groups exactly: lamp, object, light rays, screen, full shadow, partial shadow.
subject: physics
why: used for straight-line propagation, shadows and as the lead-in to eclipses

prompt: A simple unlabelled circuit diagram drawn with straight lines and right-angled corners forming one closed rectangular loop, containing a cell drawn as one long thin line beside one short thick line, a lamp drawn as a plain circle with a cross inside it, and a switch drawn as a short line hinged away from a gap. Standard circuit symbols only, no letters inside any symbol. Name the layer groups exactly: cell, lamp, switch, connecting wires.
subject: physics
why: the first circuit any electricity chapter draws, reused constantly as a base

prompt: A simple unlabelled circuit diagram drawn with straight lines and right-angled corners: one closed loop containing a cell drawn as one long thin line beside one short thick line, with the wire splitting at two junction dots into two side-by-side branches, each branch containing a lamp drawn as a plain circle with a cross inside it, before rejoining. Standard circuit symbols only, no letters inside any symbol. Name the layer groups exactly: cell, first lamp, second lamp, junctions, connecting wires.
subject: physics
why: the parallel arrangement compared against series in every circuits lesson

prompt: A simple unlabelled chart of standard electrical circuit symbols arranged in a neat grid of separate boxes, each box holding one symbol drawn in plain straight lines with a short wire stub on each side: a cell as one long thin line beside one short thick line, a battery as two cells joined, a lamp as a circle with a cross, a switch as a hinged line with a gap, a resistor as a plain rectangle, a plain empty circle for a meter, a second plain empty circle for another meter, and a resistor rectangle with a diagonal arrow across it. Every symbol must be completely empty of letters and numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: cell symbol, battery symbol, lamp symbol, switch symbol, resistor symbol, ammeter symbol, voltmeter symbol, variable resistor symbol.
subject: physics
why: the reference sheet a teacher puts on the board before any circuit-drawing task

prompt: A simple unlabelled circuit diagram drawn with straight lines and right-angled corners: a closed loop containing a cell drawn as one long thin line beside one short thick line, a lamp drawn as a circle with a cross, and a plain empty circle in the loop itself, plus a second plain empty circle connected by two wires across the two sides of the lamp only. Every circle must be completely empty of letters and numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: cell, lamp, ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel, connecting wires.
subject: physics
why: settles the perennial confusion about where each meter goes

prompt: A simple unlabelled circuit diagram drawn with straight lines and right-angled corners: a closed loop containing a cell drawn as one long thin line beside one short thick line, a rectangle with a diagonal arrow across it, a plain rectangle, and a plain empty circle in the loop, with a second plain empty circle joined by two wires across the plain rectangle only. Every circle must be completely empty of letters and numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: cell, variable resistor, test resistor, ammeter, voltmeter.
subject: physics
why: the required practical circuit for resistance and current-voltage characteristics

prompt: A simple unlabelled line graph with two plain axes crossing at a centre origin so all four quadrants are visible, carrying three separate lines through the origin: one perfectly straight sloping line, one S-shaped curve that flattens away from the origin at both ends, and one line that stays flat along the axis to the left and then rises steeply upward to the right. No numbers, no tick labels, no words. Clean thin lines. Name the layer groups exactly: horizontal axis, vertical axis, straight line, s shaped curve, diode curve, origin.
subject: physics
why: the three characteristic graphs for a resistor, a filament lamp and a diode

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a rectangular mains plug with its cover removed, showing three metal pins fixed in the casing, three separate wires running from a cable entering at the bottom to the base of each pin, a clamp holding the cable where it enters, and a small cylinder fitted in line with the wire to the top right pin. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: plug casing, live pin, neutral pin, earth pin, fuse, cable grip, cable.
subject: physics
why: the mains safety diagram every electricity chapter and every safety question uses

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a rectangular metal appliance case in cross-section with three wires entering it: one wire going to a small cylinder then on to the internal parts, one wire returning, and a third wire attached directly to the metal case and continuing down to a horizontal line with three short parallel lines beneath it decreasing in width. A hand touches the outside of the case. No shading. Name the layer groups exactly: metal case, live wire, neutral wire, earth wire, fuse, earth symbol, hand.
subject: physics
why: explains why the earth wire and fuse together make an appliance safe to touch

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram of a straight rod held in one hand while a folded cloth is rubbed along it with the other hand, with a row of small plain circles drawn along the surface of the rod and a row of small plain circles drawn on the cloth, and a short arrow between the two showing transfer. No shading, no plus or minus signs, no letters. Name the layer groups exactly: rod, cloth, hand, charges on the rod, charges on the cloth, transfer arrow.
subject: physics
why: the first demonstration in static electricity: charging by transferring electrons

prompt: A simple unlabelled line diagram showing two pairs of small balls hanging on threads from a horizontal support bar: in the left pair the two threads hang apart with the balls swung away from each other, in the right pair the threads lean inward with the balls swung close together. Curved field lines are drawn between the balls in each pair. No shading, no plus or minus signs. Name the layer groups exactly: support bar, threads, repelling balls, attracting balls, field lines.
subject: physics
why: the like-repels, unlike-attracts picture used in static and in field lessons

prompt: A simple unlabelled circuit diagram with two separate closed loops drawn one above the other using straight lines and right-angled corners: the upper loop contains a cell drawn as one long thin line beside one short thick line and two plain rectangles placed one after the other in the same wire; the lower loop contains an identical cell and two plain rectangles sitting side by side on separate branches between two junction dots.
